subject: Residency binding checklist, subprocessor sync, and temporary egress carve-out
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <legal@acmehealth.com>, Edward Cho <dpo@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Residency binding checklist, subprocessor sync, and temporary egress carve-out

Hi Maya / Edward —

Thanks for the productive call this morning. Per our discussion, I wanted to capture the immediate asks and propose next steps so we can align legal + procurement + ops. Key items you raised:

- Confirm that Redwood will provide an EU residency binding (data exclusively kept in EU region) for production PII workloads, with a documented failover window for transient cross-region processing.
- Provide an up-to-date subprocessor roster and clarify which subprocessors may process data outside the EU during short failover windows.
- Share a DPA addendum with language around pinning, failover windows (duration/notification), and audit evidence (SOC 2 + relevant logs).

Proposed next steps:
1) Marissa will circulate a draft DPA addendum and the current subprocessor roster by end of day today.
2) We'll call out the default transient egress window and an elevated option for customers requiring longer notice.
3) Schedule a 1-hour technical session with our ops team to walk the failover mechanics and telemetry available to Acme.

If that looks right I’ll mark action items and set a tentative calendar invite.

Thanks —
Sergio
Sergio Alvarez | Account Executive
Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0178

Attachments: none in this initial note.

From: Maya Patel <legal@acmehealth.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Edward Cho <dpo@acmehealth.com>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2026 11:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Residency binding checklist, subprocessor sync, and temporary egress carve-out

Sergio —

Appreciate the recap. A few clarifying questions before we accept the proposed path:

1) Residency binding: We need explicit DPA language that (a) designates the EU as the default processing region for Acme production workloads, (b) prohibits routine cross-border processing, and (c) limits transient cross-region processing to specific, enumerated scenarios (failover, maintenance, emergency).

2) Failover window: Please confirm Redwood's standard maximum transient egress duration and whether you offer a longer, contractually-bound option (e.g., 96 hours) for customers in regulated spaces. Also confirm required customer notification cadence and whether logs/telemetry will be made available for inspection.

3) Subprocessors: We require a CSV-style roster with current subprocessors, their primary function, and the location(s) where they operate. Specifically call out if any model hosting, telemetry, analytics, or third-party observability providers could process data outside the EU during a failover.

4) Evidence: Please include SOC 2 report status and the mechanism for providing audit-read access or summaries (redacted as needed).

Could you send your proposed addendum + roster? I attached a short note with our negotiation points (Acme-DPA-Questions.docx) for your reference. Also, procurement will need a tentative DocuSign flow and an estimated procurement timeline.

Thanks —
Maya Patel
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Acme Health, Inc.
legal@acmehealth.com

Attachment referenced: Acme-DPA-Questions.docx (see cover note)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <legal@acmehealth.com>, Edward Cho <dpo@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2026 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency binding checklist, subprocessor sync, and temporary egress carve-out

Thanks Maya — sending the draft materials and short answers below. Per Sergio's note I pulled in ops (Kimberly) and product (Jordan) for any technical clarifications.

Short answers (high level):
- Residency binding: Redwood can offer an EU residency binding via our Dedicated or Private deployment options. For Hosted customers we provide strong region affinity and documented controls but Hosted does not provide a legally-binding geo-custody guarantee unless included in a DPA addendum.

- Failover window: Our standard transient egress policy for production failover is up to 72 hours (automated re-sync and rollback expected to complete within this window). We can offer an extended 96-hour contractual option for regulated customers. Notification: we provide immediate alerting on failover start + a follow-up incident report within 24 hours with telemetry. Audit evidence: per-customer logs and tokenized traces can be provided via a secure share for agreed audits.

- Subprocessors: attached is the current roster (subprocessor_roster_2026-08.csv). Highlights: cloud provider (eu-west-1 region primary), model weights hosting partner (Redwood-managed - EU regional hosts), telemetry/metrics partner (aggregated, EU-hosted; US fallback only for emergency diagnostics), analytics vendor (may process anonymized metadata in US for aggregate analytics; not PII). Any failover to non-EU locations is limited to the transient window and documented in the incident report.

- Evidence: attached is a DPA addendum draft (DPA-Addendum_Redwood_v1.pdf) covering the pinning language, failover scenarios, notification commitments, and an SLA option for extended egress windows. We will provide SOC 2 summary + instructions to request a secure read-only download for the full report.

Next steps proposed:
1) Please review the attached addendum and roster and flag redlines.
2) If language looks reasonable, we'll prepare a DocuSign packet (link included below) and target procurement signature within 2 weeks.
3) Kimberly will host a 1-hour ops deep-dive this Thursday 10:00-11:00 AM CET — calendar invite to follow.

Related links: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/12345/ACME-RDW-2109 (deal record), draft DocuSign packet: https://app.docusign.com/prepare/REDWOOD_ACME_DPA

Attachments: DPA-Addendum_Redwood_v1.pdf; subprocessor_roster_2026-08.csv

Best —
Marissa Cole | Legal Ops, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Residency binding checklist, subprocessor sync, and temporary egress carve-out

All —

Thank you for the quick turnaround on the DPA addendum and roster. A couple of operational follow-ups from the DPO perspective before we proceed to signature:

- We want a short, written runbook that enumerates exactly which triggers allow a transient cross-region hop (e.g., primary availability zone failure, critical security incident, maintenance with no regional capacity). Could Redwood provide a 1-2 page runbook excerpt that Acme can reference in the addendum?

- Telemetry delivery: can we get an example export format for the incident report and the tokenized trace you mentioned? Procurement expects to see sample output ahead of signature.

If Redwood can share both items, procurement will proceed to DocuSign and we can schedule the ops call.

Best regards —
Edward Cho | DPO, Acme Health

Marissa / team —

This looks good and addresses our core concerns. Procurement is comfortable moving to DocuSign once we get the short runbook excerpt and a sample incident export. Two small requests before signature:

- Add a sentence to Section 2.1 of the addendum explicitly listing the triggers that may cause transient cross-region processing (we'll accept the list you proposed in the runbook excerpt).
- Confirm the extended 96-hour option will be available as a checked box in the DocuSign packet and that pricing impact will be shown on the procurement page.

Assuming you can push the runbook excerpt + sample export to the drive link, procurement will start routing DocuSign today. We will also schedule the ops deep-dive — Thursday 10:00-11:00 CET works for our team.

Thanks —
Maya Patel
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Acme Health, Inc.
